newsitem.title: FRANCE: French truckers block roads for third day in row.
newsitem.headline: French truckers block roads for third day in row.

text.p: Truckers seeking higher pay, retirement at age 55 and shorter working hours tied up traffic around major French cities on Wednesday for the third day in a row.

By slowing down, using roadblocks or using their lorries to physically block other vehicles, the truckers obstructed access roads and major highways around the central city of Lyon, Bordeaux in southwestern France and Lille in the north.

They also disrupted traffic in and around Avignon, Nimes, Montpelier and Toulouse in southern France and shut down a main road between the central cities of Saint Etienne and Clermont-Ferrand, the authorities said.
The truckers again blocked off a key bridge connecting France and Germany over the river Rhine at Strasbourg by parking trucks on either side of the border.
Also cut off was a Royal Dutch/Shell refinery in Berre just outside the southern port city of Marseille.
Five trade unions and the independent FNCR truckers' federation called a third day of protests after talks with government officials failed to resolve the dispute.
